text: {"standards":[{"code":"W.6.2","verdict":"partly","reason":"In Part B, students write one comparison paragraph with a topic sentence, evidence from both texts, and a concluding statement, but this is a brief paragraph rather than an extended informative text that develops a topic through sustained selection and analysis."},{"code":"W.6.4","verdict":"taught","reason":"The Literacy Lab and Part B direct students to revise for formal style, transitions, and organization appropriate to a comparison paragraph for a school audience."},{"code":"RL.6.1","verdict":"taught","reason":"In Part A, students annotate and cite details from Chapter 22 and the Odyssey excerpt, then infer what each homecoming says about home."},{"code":"RL.6.2","verdict":"partly","reason":"Students identify the idea of home conveyed through details in Part A, but no activity has them state a theme in full or write an objective summary separate from opinion."},{"code":"RL.6.9","verdict":"taught","reason":"Part A's three-column chart and Part B's paragraph have students compare how the Odyssey excerpt and The Lightning Thief treat the shared theme of homecoming."},{"code":"L.6.1","verdict":"taught","reason":"The Literacy Lab has students fix run-on sentences, subject-verb agreement, and informal word choice, and the Part B checklist asks them to revise for conventional English."},{"code":"L.6.1.e","verdict":"taught","reason":"The Literacy Lab has students identify slang and run-ons as variations from standard English and apply named revision strategies such as replacing words and splitting run-ons."}],"anchorText":{"verdict":"uses","reason":"Part A directs students to reread Chapter 22 (pp. 370-375) and the Odyssey Book 13 excerpt, the two texts the Outline names."}}
